Chapter 12: Returning to the Beginning—The Circle of Practice.
After years of training and countless hours of practice, have you ever noticed how you end up right back where you started? The basics that once seemed so tough now come naturally. Your mind, which used to dart around restlessly, feels calm and steady.
It’s funny, isn’t it? The journey isn’t a straight line at all—it’s a circle, always returning to the beginning.
Picture the dojo for a moment. The master, after decades of experience, goes right back to the simplest forms, practicing them with the same focus as a beginner. There’s no ego, no sense of arrival—just a deep appreciation for those fundamentals. That’s the real foundation, the thing that holds everything else up. The mind stays humble, open, always ready to learn.
And you know, it’s not just about martial arts. Most of us, as we go through life, realize that the deepest lessons are usually the simplest: paying attention, being present, showing kindness. The teachings of the unfettered mind invite us all to come back—again and again—to those basics. The breath. The body. This moment, right now.
Think about a parent who’s spent years raising kids. What really matters in the end? Just being there—listening, caring, showing up. Or a leader who’s hustled for years, only to discover that the real challenge is being present, meeting every moment with humility and openness.
The truth is, the journey never really ends. There’s always something new to learn, another layer to let go of, more room to open your heart.
For the swordsman, this means always returning to the basics—the core of practice. For the rest of us, it’s about coming back to the simple things: the breath, the body, the present. The path is a circle, always coming back, always deepening.
And that’s how the teachings of the unfettered mind become more than a lesson—they become a way of life. A practice that never truly ends. A journey that, in a beautiful way, is always just beginning.
